title: PDMD: Projected Distribution Matching Distillation for Video Diffusion Models
why_read: A focused technical fix for a known instability problem in fast video-generation model distillation, with concrete before/after benchmark gains.
analysis: Distribution Matching Distillation speeds up video diffusion models by cutting the number of denoising steps needed, but the paper explains that a known failure mode causes errors to accumulate and degrade image quality during training. PDMD adds a mathematically justified correction, a projection step, that filters out a systematic part of this error using only a small code change. It shows measurable improvements on standard video-generation benchmarks (VBench, VideoGen-Eval) across both a large video model and a joint video-audio model, and requires no new losses, networks, or extra training stages. This is a useful, low-overhead engineering fix rather than a flashy new architecture, which is why it's a solid moderate-interest item mainly for people working directly on generative video models.
